# rmux 0.1.13 — preview
This release improves project commands, Settings, and keyboard focus.
## Project and editor workflows
- Configured commands accept `{project_dir}` as a complete argument. Your VS Code return shortcut can target the original project even after changing terminal directories or renaming the workspace. - Local commands that open a dedicated build or test workspace retain that project identity. Both command pickers preview the resolved target and explain missing project context. - Settings includes a VS Code editor configuration example and an option to open the settings file without the configured editor, useful when repairing its path.
## Interface and navigation
- Sidebar directory labels show the folder name, with the full path in the tooltip. - Settings has a compact footer with two aligned rows of actions. - Opening the command palette from an inspector restores terminal context. Shortcuts, configured commands and layout pickers use that same context. - Palette search keeps command abbreviations while avoiding unrelated matches from scattered letters in long paths. - Pull-request lookup prefers open PRs and reports ambiguous matches instead of choosing an arbitrary result.
## Performance
- Bash and zsh reuse encoded working-directory text between prompts when the directory has not changed. Prompt and directory reporting still runs on every prompt.
## Downloads and validation
GitHub builds the signed and notarized macOS Apple Silicon DMG and ZIP, Linux x86-64 tarball, and Windows x86-64 ZIP. macOS updates use Sparkle.
Focused matcher, configured-command, Settings, PR lookup and shell-integration checks passed during development. Native review covered the compact Settings layout and Settings → command palette → next terminal focus. Broader native interaction, multi-window VS Code focus, and Windows runtime validation remain pending. Automatic Bash login integration remains unsupported.
[VS Code setup](https://rmux.app/vscode/) · [Browser demo](https://rmux.app)
